::: {.callout-important}
## Have you created a repository for your capstone project?
A pre-requisite for this homework is that you created a repository for your capstone project. This was an assignment of module 5. If you haven't yet, please work through the steps outlined in [Assignment 1 of Module 5](../md-05/am-05-1-project-data.qmd) before you start with the steps outlined here.
:::

## Step 1: Create a new folder for processed data

1. Open the [Content]{.highlight-yellow} tab of the ds4owd-002 workspace on Posit Cloud: [{{< var platforms.posit-cloud >}}/content/all?sort=name_asc]({{< var platforms.posit-cloud >}}/content/all?sort=name_asc)

2. Open your capstone project by clicking on it. The project name starts with `project-USERNAME` where `USERNAME` is your GitHub username.

3. Navigate to the [Files]{.highlight-yellow} tab in the bottom right window of RStudio.

4. Click on the `data` folder in the bottom right window.

::: {.callout-tip}
If you don't have a `data` folder yet, create it first by clicking the [New Folder]{.highlight-yellow} button and naming it `data`.
:::

5. Click on the [New Folder]{.highlight-yellow} button to create a new folder.

6. Enter the name [processed]{.highlight-yellow} in the field and click [OK]{.highlight-yellow}.

7. Click on the new `processed` folder in the bottom right window to open it.

## Step 2: Create a `README.md` file

1. Make sure you are in the `data/processed` folder in the [Files]{.highlight-yellow} tab (bottom right window of RStudio).

2. Click on the [Blank File]{.highlight-yellow} button (with a plus icon) to create a new file.

3. Select the option [Text File]{.highlight-yellow}.

4. Enter the name [README.md]{.highlight-yellow} in the field and click [OK]{.highlight-yellow}.

5. Open this link in a new browser tab: [{{< var course.github-org >}}/metadata-readme-template]({{< var course.github-org >}}/metadata-readme-template/blob/main/README.md)

6. Click on the [Raw]{.highlight-yellow} button in the top right corner of the file view to see the raw markdown content.

7. Select all the content (Ctrl+A on Windows or Cmd+A on Mac) and copy it (Ctrl+C or Cmd+C).

8. Return to your Posit Cloud project and paste the content into the empty `README.md` file you created in the `data/processed` folder.

9. Save the file by clicking [File]{.highlight-yellow} > [Save]{.highlight-yellow} or using Ctrl+S (Cmd+S on Mac).

10. Commit this change:
    - Navigate to the [Git]{.highlight-yellow} pane in the top-right window of RStudio
    - Check the box next to `README.md` to stage it
    - Click [Commit]{.highlight-yellow}
    - Enter commit message: `add README template to processed data folder`
    - Click [Commit]{.highlight-yellow} and then [Close]{.highlight-yellow}

## Step 3: Create a data dictionary

1. Open a spreadsheet tool of your choice (Microsoft Excel, Google Sheets, or LibreOffice Calc).

2. Create a new spreadsheet and add two column names in the first row:
   - `variable_name`
   - `description`

3. You do not need to describe all variables yet. Start with at least 3-5 key variables from your dataset.

4. Save the file as [dictionary.xlsx]{.highlight-yellow} on your computer.

5. Also save the file as a CSV by selecting [File]{.highlight-yellow} > [Save As]{.highlight-yellow} or [Export]{.highlight-yellow}, then choose [CSV]{.highlight-yellow} format and name it [dictionary.csv]{.highlight-yellow}.

::: {.callout-tip}
## Working with your data dictionary

When you need to edit your data dictionary in the future:
1. Edit the `.xlsx` file in your spreadsheet software
2. Export/save it as `.csv` again
3. Re-upload the updated `.csv` file to your Posit Cloud project folder
:::

## Step 4: Upload the dictionary

1. Return to your capstone project on Posit Cloud: [{{< var platforms.posit-cloud >}}/content/all?sort=name_asc]({{< var platforms.posit-cloud >}}/content/all?sort=name_asc)

2. Navigate to the [Files]{.highlight-yellow} tab in the bottom right window.

3. Navigate to the `data/processed` folder by clicking on it.

4. Click the [Upload]{.highlight-yellow} button (with an up arrow icon).

5. Click [Choose File]{.highlight-yellow}, select your `dictionary.csv` file, and click [OK]{.highlight-yellow}.

::: {.callout-warning}
Upload only the `.csv` version of your dictionary to your project. The `.xlsx` file should remain on your local computer for editing purposes.
:::

6. Commit this change:
    - Navigate to the [Git]{.highlight-yellow} pane in the top-right window of RStudio
    - Check the box next to `dictionary.csv` to stage it
    - Click [Commit]{.highlight-yellow}
    - Enter commit message: `add data dictionary for processed data`
    - Click [Commit]{.highlight-yellow} and then [Close]{.highlight-yellow}

## Step 5: Prepare your analysis-ready (processed) data

::: {.callout-important}
## Start now, iterate later

[It's important to start this step now]{.highlight-yellow}, even if your data preparation is not perfect yet. This step will involve several iterations, depending on the complexity of your raw data. For this homework assignment, create a first version so that we can start evaluating the complexity of your project.
:::

1. Open the `index.qmd` file in your capstone project on Posit Cloud.

2. Add a code chunk at the beginning of your document to load the necessary R packages:

````markdown
```{{r}}
library(tidyverse)
library(here)
```
````

3. In a new code chunk, import your raw data. In this example we are using a CSV file:

````markdown
```{{r}}
raw_data <- read_csv(here::here("data/raw/your-file-name.csv"))
```
````

4. Write code to bring your data into a state where it's ready for analysis. For example:
   - Rename columns with `rename()`
   - Select columns that are relevant with `select()`
   - Remove missing values with `filter()` or `drop_na()`
   - Join several dataframes with `left_join()`, `right_join()`, etc.
   - Create new variables with `mutate()`

5. Once you have your data in a state where it's ready for analysis, save it as a CSV file in the `data/processed` folder:

````markdown
```{{r}}
processed_data <- raw_data |>
  select(column1, column2, column3) |>
  filter(!is.na(column1)) |>
  rename(new_name = old_name)

write_csv(processed_data,
          here::here("data/processed/my-processed-data.csv"))
```
````

::: {.callout-tip}
Replace `my-processed-data.csv` with a descriptive name for your processed dataset. This is the file that your data dictionary should describe.
:::

6. Commit these changes:
    - Navigate to the [Git]{.highlight-yellow} pane in the top-right window of RStudio
    - Check the boxes next to `index.qmd` and your processed data file to stage them
    - Click [Commit]{.highlight-yellow}
    - Enter commit message: `create processed data and update analysis document`
    - Click [Commit]{.highlight-yellow} and then [Close]{.highlight-yellow}

## Step 6: Push your changes to GitHub

You have made several commits in the previous steps. Now it's time to push all of these commits to GitHub.

1. Navigate to the [Git]{.highlight-yellow} pane in the top-right window of RStudio.
2. Click on the [Push]{.highlight-yellow} button (with an up arrow icon).
3. Enter your GitHub username and click [OK]{.highlight-yellow}.
4. Enter your GitHub Personal Access Token (PAT) in the field and click [OK]{.highlight-yellow}. This is the personal access token you created in Module 1.

If you see a message that says `HEAD -> main`, then you have successfully pushed your changes to the remote repository on GitHub. Click Close. [If you do not see this message]{.highlight-yellow}, make sure you have entered your GitHub username and GitHub PAT correctly.


## Step 7: Open an issue on GitHub

1. Open <https://github.com/> in your browser.
2. Navigate to the GitHub organization for the course: [{{< var course.github-org >}}]({{< var course.github-org >}})
3. Find the repository `project-USERNAME` that [ends with your GitHub username]{.highlight-yellow}, and open it by clicking on the repository name.
   - Replace `USERNAME` with your actual GitHub username.

::: {.callout-tip}
You can search for your repository by typing your username in the search bar just below the Repository heading.
:::

4. You can verify here that your changes have been pushed to the remote repository by looking at the commit messages and files in your project.
5. Click on the [Issues]{.highlight-yellow} tab.
6. Click on the green [New issue]{.highlight-yellow} button.
7. In the [Title]{.highlight-yellow} field write: [Prepared first iteration of analysis-ready (processed) data]{.highlight-yellow}.
8. In the [Leave a comment]{.highlight-yellow} field, tag the course instructors `@seawaR` `@larnsce` and briefly describe what you've added (README, dictionary, processed data).
9. Scroll down the page and click the green [Submit new issue]{.highlight-yellow} button.

Congratulations! You have completed the project metadata documentation assignment.
